title: EXCEPT
description: Learn how to use the EXCEPT operator to subtract the result set of one query from another, returning distinct rows that appear only in the first query.

data.text: The SQL Server EXCEPT compares the result sets of two queries and returns the distinct rows from the first query that are not output by the second query. In other words, the EXCEPT operator subtracts the result set of a query from another.

data.title: EXCEPT Syntax
data.content: Returns rows from query_1 that are not in query_2.

data.text: The following are the rules for combining the result sets of two queries in the above syntax:

items: The number and order of columns must be the same in both queries.
The data types of the corresponding columns must be the same or compatible.

data.text: The EXCEPT of two result sets T1 and T2 returns the distinct row(s) from T1 that do not appear in T2.

data.title: Find Products with No Sales
data.content: Subtract product IDs that have sales from all product IDs.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id
FROM
    production.products
EXCEPT
SELECT
    product_id
FROM
    sales.order_items;

data.text: In this example, the first query returns all the products. The second query returns the products that have sales. Therefore, the result set includes only the products that have no sales.
To sort the result set created by the EXCEPT operator, add the ORDER BY clause to the last query:

data.title: EXCEPT with ORDER BY
data.content: Sort products with no sales by product_id ascending.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id
FROM
    production.products
EXCEPT
SELECT
    product_id
FROM
    sales.order_items
ORDER BY
    product_id;

data.title: EXCEPT vs NOT IN
data.text: EXCEPT is similar to NOT IN but handles NULL values differently. EXCEPT treats NULL as equal to NULL for comparison purposes, while NOT IN with a NULL in the list returns an empty result set.

data.alt: SQL Server EXCEPT with ORDER BY example

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: EXCEPT subtracts the result set of the second query from the first query.
It returns distinct rows from the first query not present in the second.
Columns must match in count, order, and compatible data types.
Add ORDER BY to the last query to sort the EXCEPT result set.
EXCEPT is useful for finding differences between two data sets.
